title: Biographical data; family origins
description: Bernice Sullivan provides her birth date and place in Adams, Massachusetts, and details her parents' backgrounds, including her mother Helen Mogul's marriage in 1926 and the family's farm life. She also names her siblings and their current locations.

title: Marriage; children; education and teaching
description: Sullivan discusses meeting her husband Mike and their 1958 marriage, noting their children's births and that Mike delivered them at the hospital. She outlines her education in university medicine and her six-year teaching career in St. Mary's and Plummer before becoming a full-time farm wife.

title: Rural life philosophy; 4-H and childhood
description: Sullivan champions raising children in rural areas to develop work ethic and responsibility through animal care and chores. She compares her own 4-H experiences in Massachusetts, including trips to Boston and West Virginia, with her children's current participation.

title: Teaching career; marriage history; childbirth
description: She elaborates on teaching English, history, and home economics, and coaching basketball in Plummer. She also recounts meeting Mike through 4-H and his unconventional role delivering their children at the hospital.

title: Gardening; food preservation; livestock
description: Sullivan describes their large garden with experimental peanuts and okra, companion planting methods, and food preservation using an electric dehydrator. She details raising Montadale sheep, dairy cows, chickens, and other livestock, including birthing difficulties and butchering practices.

title: Doctor's wife; church; household management
description: She reflects on being a doctor's wife in a small community, past Sunday school teaching, and the children's involvement in the Nazarene Church music program. She also covers limited television habits and the family's busy schedule of chores and 4-H work.

title: Preparedness; neighborhood cooperation; self-sufficiency
description: Sullivan explains the family's emergency preparedness, including storing honey and detergent, growing all their food, and teaching the children survival skills like sewing and gardening. She details their neighborhood trading network with mechanics and beekeepers, and hosting community Fourth of July and Christmas gatherings at their farmhouse.

title: Hunting and fishing; basketball
description: Bernice Sullivan says her husband Mike neither hunts nor fishes, while the children do a little; she proudly recounts Kent killing the family's sheep after gun safety classes. She adds that winter hunting conflicts with basketball, and she herself played and coached basketball rather than skiing or skating.

title: School sports; education comparison
description: She recalls women's basketball existing in Plummer when she arrived to teach. She compares her children's education with her own, noting greater travel and broader opportunities through science fairs, debate, and music, though the basic curriculum is similar.

title: New education ideas; school construction
description: She approves of new educational ideas for average students but worries about repetitiveness for struggling ones and lack of programs for accelerated learners. She recounts chairing the 1973 school bond committee, criticizing delays, site changes, and the use of churches for overcrowded classes.

title: Transportation; music lessons
description: She describes the daily driving to get children to practices and lessons, and notes that Todd will soon drive a jeep. The children all play instruments, and she explains the difficulty of coordinating family music and her belief that music builds discipline and athletic ability.

title: 4-H skills; food preservation
description: She mentions the boys making shirts and learning cooking and sewing through 4-H. The family cans and dehydrates food, including making jerky from a whole lamb using a dehydrator.

title: Recording plans; community life
description: Dale Anderson explains the tapes will be archived at the Women's Center for researchers and relatives. They praise the friendly, satisfied people in the area, and Bernice says she values the town's educational and living advantages for her children.

title: Women's Center talk; self-sufficiency
description: Dale invites Bernice to speak at a Women's Center brown bag series about rural life, and she agrees for autumn. She discusses becoming less dependent on stores and mentions survival literature, including books from inflation survival sources.

title: Gardening
description: She describes her oldest son's interest in wild plants and his ambition to be a landscape architect. She recounts their first garden year experiments with companion planting and the discovery that sunflowers improved cucumber germination.
